title: A Marc Benioff-backed startup thinks AI can solve the AI deployment problem
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: June emerged from stealth today with a $20 million pre-seed round to make AI adoption simpler.
body:
A new startup, June, co-founded by former Salesforce executives Efrat Rapoport, Ohad Hen, Barak Goldstein, and Idan Tsitiat, has emerged from stealth with $20 million in pre-seed funding, led by Marc Benioff's Time Ventures. June aims to revolutionize how large enterprises deploy AI, addressing the current paradox where AI's complexity often necessitates extensive professional services and a growing workforce of "forward-deployed engineers" to get systems operational. The team, previously behind Bonobo AI, recognized this significant bottleneck after observing customers struggle with AI integration at Salesforce.

June's core innovation lies in simplifying the integration of AI models with the intricate, often messy, reality of enterprise legacy systems. While building an AI agent template might be straightforward, the real challenge, according to Rapoport, is making it function reliably amidst fragmented data across platforms like Salesforce, ServiceNow, and DataBricks, complex workflows, and years of technical debt. June's technology is designed to navigate these complexities, enabling AI agents to understand and operate effectively even when faced with issues like duplicate database fields or inconsistent data usage across different teams.

This initiative is crucial for developers and researchers as it tackles one of the most significant hurdles to AI adoption: practical deployment and value realization within existing corporate infrastructure. By providing a more streamlined approach to connect AI agents with disparate data sources and workflows, June could dramatically reduce the need for costly, bespoke integration efforts. This shift would allow developers and researchers to focus more on AI innovation itself, accelerating the pace at which AI solutions can be brought to market and deliver tangible business value, moving beyond the current reliance on extensive human intervention for implementation.
